fact_check.claim: New transfers must live on campus for one academic year unless they already met the requirement elsewhere
fact_check.note: Page says new transfers who have not met the requirement at a previous institution must live on campus for one academic year.

fact_check.claim: Spring transfers live on campus for the spring semester plus the following academic year
fact_check.note: Transfer page: spring transfers are required to live on campus for the incoming spring semester as well as the following academic year.

fact_check.claim: Living on campus requires a meal plan; rate page does not price it
fact_check.note: Residence hall residents must enroll in a university meal plan; the rate page lists no meal plan prices.

fact_check.claim: Exemptions: two years on campus at previous school, or matriculating as junior or senior
fact_check.note: Both listed as not subject to the residency requirement.

fact_check.claim: Exemption is requested by logging in to the Housing application and applying for the exemption term while open, not after a signed license
fact_check.note: Residential policy says exactly this; supporting documentation may be required, which fits 'keep proof handy'.

fact_check.claim: Requirement applies to first-year and transfer students who arrived in fall 2022 or later
fact_check.note: Page: applies beginning with first-year and transfer students arriving in fall 2022.

fact_check.claim: The 2026-27 new student application opens April 1 (no time given)
fact_check.note: Opens April 1; no time listed for new students. The noon time applies only to graduate/professional students and is no longer in the article.

fact_check.claim: Newly admitted students need an activated NetID to apply
fact_check.note: Page confirms the ten-day NetID advice but the fetch summary did not separately quote the 'need an activated NetID' wording. Low risk; source normally works.

fact_check.claim: Transfer students should apply within ten days of receiving the NetID (framed as advice, not a deadline)
fact_check.note: Page: transfer students should also apply within ten days of receiving their NetID. The article now calls it advice and no longer claims it keeps you off the waitlist.

fact_check.claim: Confirmations begin in mid-June: a building and room, or the guaranteed waitlist with weekly updates
fact_check.note: Confirmed on the page.

fact_check.claim: Transfers may be placed in the West Campus House System, South Campus Residence Halls, North Campus Residence Halls and Program Houses
fact_check.note: The application page (not the transfer page) lists North Campus; the article attributes it to the application page. Search snippet of the page gives the same wording.

fact_check.claim: Transfer rooms are grouped together whenever possible; in limited situations transfers who qualify as first-year are placed in first-year residences
fact_check.note: Both sentences are on the transfer page.

fact_check.claim: West Campus: Alice Cook, Carl Becker, Flora Rose, Hans Bethe, William Keeton
fact_check.note: Matches the transfer page list.

fact_check.claim: Townhouse Apartments appear on Cornell's transfer housing list (no longer under West Campus)
fact_check.note: Listed as its own entry.

fact_check.claim: South Campus: Cascadilla Hall, Schuyler House, Sheldon Court, 112 Edgemoor, 104 Mary Ann Wood Drive, 109 McGraw Place
fact_check.note: Matches exactly.

fact_check.claim: Program Houses are themed halls for first-year and upper-level students; Equity & Engagement Community is upper-level only
fact_check.note: Transfer page: Program Houses are for first-year and upper-level students; the program houses page says EEC is upper-level students only.

fact_check.claim: Join a Program House by listing it as a preference and acknowledging its mission; examples Risley, HILC, Loving House
fact_check.note: All three houses are listed and the joining steps match.

fact_check.claim: More than 500 first-year and transfer students live in Program Houses each year
fact_check.note: Page says over 500 first-year and transfer students will live in Program Houses.

fact_check.claim: Double costs $6,872 per semester in 2026-27 ($13,744 a year)
fact_check.note: Fall and spring both $6,872; annual total $13,744.

fact_check.claim: Triple or one-room quad $6,322 per semester ($12,644 a year)
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Single or townhouse double $7,783 per semester ($15,566 a year)
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Super single $8,298 per semester ($16,595 a year)
fact_check.note: Matches. The table still omits the quad ($6,872 per semester), which the earlier review asked to add; it is an omission, not a wrong fact.

fact_check.claim: Rates include gas, electricity, garbage pickup and internet up to 200 GB a month
fact_check.note: Stated in the page's general rate information (the page does not say whether co-op rates include these).

fact_check.claim: Eight co-ops, among the least expensive options on campus; most have singles and doubles, four have meal plans, all have shared kitchens
fact_check.note: All details match.

fact_check.claim: Co-op singles $3,949 to $6,014 and doubles $3,487 to $4,981 per semester
fact_check.note: Single range runs from Red Bud $3,949 to Wari $6,014; double range from $3,487 to $4,981. The $5,693 maximum in the earlier fix list was a partial reading; the article's $6,014 is correct.

fact_check.claim: Co-op page says co-ops are for transfer students and undergraduates after their first semester; transfer page says upper-level students only
fact_check.note: Both wordings confirmed on the two pages; the article flags the conflict and tells readers to ask the house.

fact_check.claim: Co-op selection usually starts in early February and rolls after that; Housing Office 607-255-5368
fact_check.note: Both on the co-op page.

fact_check.claim: Applicants can request a single, double, triple or quad; Cornell will do its best
fact_check.note: Quoted: 'may request to live in a single, double, triple, or quad'; 'We will do our best to assign you to your preferred room type.'

fact_check.claim: Roommate: short lifestyle questionnaire or name a specific student; not guaranteed
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: New transfers cannot cancel a housing assignment; fee schedule ($50 through Jan 31 up to $2,000 July 1 to Aug 15) is for returning juniors and seniors
fact_check.note: Page says transfers cannot cancel unless no longer attending or exempt; fee schedule applies to returning juniors and seniors.

fact_check.claim: No-show rule: not checked in by first day of classes without late-arrival arrangement means cancellation and 50 percent of the fall semester room rate
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Fall 2025: timeslot deadline August 1, new students moved in August 18 and 19; no 2026 schedule posted
fact_check.note: Dates match and are labeled as 2025; page says to check back for Fall 2026.

fact_check.claim: Room change application open select times in fall and spring; Room Swap windows; new transfers swap only with sophomores, juniors, seniors
fact_check.note: Page says Sophomores, Juniors, Seniors and New Transfers can only swap with each other; first-years swap only with first-years.

fact_check.claim: All first-year students are guaranteed on-campus housing; transfer page does not use the word guarantee
fact_check.note: Guarantee for first-years confirmed; no guarantee wording on the transfer page.

fact_check.claim: Momofthree24 says transfers are placed after current students and many went to Cascadilla and Schuyler; HopefulHotelieMom says most transfers get West Campus and disputes last pick
fact_check.note: Both posts match; attributed to individual posters as one-year snapshots, with no hard fact resting on them.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Daily Sun 2016: some transfers temporarily housed in North Campus lounges
fact_check.note: About 30 transfers were put in converted lounges in Jameson and High Rise 5.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Daily Sun 2018: transfers had no housing guarantee and some learned their assignment in June
fact_check.note: Article says Cornell does not guarantee transfer housing and that transfers learned on June 22.

beats_top.why: Cornell's application page is short and leaves out the rule, the 2026-27 rates, the co-op prices, exemptions and the cancellation trap. Our opening paragraph gives the one-year rule, the ten-day advice, placement options and the $6,872 double in one place, then a timeline and rate table.
changes: Optional: add the quad ($6,872 per semester) to the rate table, for example by labeling the row 'Double or quad'.
Optional: add the Housing Office contact (607-255-5368, housing@cornell.edu) to the exemptions paragraph.
